items.followUp: What happens to the DNA content and chromosome number during S-phase?

rubric.why: S-phase includes DNA replication, so each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids.
rubric.description: DNA replicates, producing two sister chromatids for each chromosome.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is replicated and chromosomes form two sister chromatids.

rubric.why: The amount of DNA doubles during S-phase, but the chromosome number does not change.
rubric.description: DNA content doubles while chromosome number remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the chromosome number stays the same, or that DNA doubles without a change in chromosome number.

modelAnswer: During S-phase, DNA replicates and each chromosome forms two sister chromatids.
The DNA content doubles, but the chromosome number remains unchanged.

items.followUp: Define synapsis and state the stage of meiosis in which it occurs.

rubric.why: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.description: Homologous chromosomes pair with each other.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining synapsis as the pairing or coming together of homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: Synapsis occurs during prophase I, specifically in zygotene.
rubric.description: It occurs during prophase I of meiosis, in the zygotene stage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying prophase I or zygotene.

modelAnswer: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis, specifically in zygotene.

items.followUp: What is the effect of an unsuitable temperature on an enzyme?

accept: shape of the active site changes
rubric.why: Denaturation changes an enzyme's structure, including the shape of its active site.
rubric.description: The enzyme's structure or active-site shape changes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that denaturation changes the enzyme's structure or shape, particularly its active site.

rubric.why: The changed active site means the enzyme can no longer catalyse its reaction normally.
rubric.description: The enzyme loses its catalytic activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the denatured enzyme loses activity or can no longer catalyse the reaction.

modelAnswer: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme's structure that alters the shape of its active site.
As a result, the enzyme loses its catalytic activity.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cofactor and a coenzyme.

rubric.why: A prosthetic group is firmly attached to its enzyme.
rubric.description: A prosthetic group is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a prosthetic group as tightly, permanently, or firmly bound to an enzyme.

rubric.why: A coenzyme is less firmly attached and can separate from the enzyme.
rubric.description: A coenzyme is loosely or temporarily bound and can dissociate from the enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a coenzyme as loosely or temporarily bound, or able to dissociate.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component that is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
A coenzyme is an organic non-protein component that is loosely bound and can dissociate from the enzyme.
